body:
Review-and-fix pass over the current head (242a597), together with web-platform-tests/wpt#64909. ### Questions / follow-ups - Creating `newElement` now happens between computing `(target, refNode)` from `commonAncestor` and inserting `lastNode` there. For a customized built-in formatting element with a defined `is` (outside the fragment case), that runs the constructor at that point, with `furthestBlock` still at its original position. The existing conditions on `refNode`, the abort flag, and `target`'s element child cover the tree-shape hazards, and the PR body calls out the ordering change, but if script in that constructor moves `target` itself, `lastNode` is inserted into a stale `target`. The rest of the tree builder has the same property (insertion into whatever the current node is), so I left it; flagging in case you would rather compute the insertion location after `newElement` is created (the `pendingRedirects` update would move with it). - The note on the inner-loop clone says `commonAncestor`'s node document and registry can differ from `node`'s when `commonAncestor` is a `template`. In the template case only the registry differs (both are in the template contents owner document), while the document differs in the removed-formatting-element case. The collective phrasing reads fine to me; mentioning in case you want to split it. - Chrome Canary's inner-loop clone of a formatting element whose token has an `is` attribute disappearing (test 6) reproduces without a sanitizer (`

`); Firefox matches the spec. I can file that against Blink>HTML>Parser and link it from the implementation-bugs checklist if you want. ### Findings All three commits trace correctly through the six tests in the companion WPT (each expected result follows from the algorithm as written), `create an element for a token` and `insert a foreign element` pass the registries and documents the fixes rely on, and DOM's *adopt* indeed only ever assigns the global registry, so the propagation step before insertion is needed. The build is clean and the algorithm checker reports nothing new in the changed range. Two non-normative fixes, pushed to this branch: - 861bb60: `For each` over inclusive descendants, which are not an Infra list; the other tree-order iterations in the spec (`get HTML-aware text content`, `CustomElementRegistry`'s `initialize()`, and the autofocus delegate) use a plain "For each". - e3c2ecc: the note next to the registry propagation said `lastNode` and its descendants were created with `formattingElement` or one of its clones as their intended parent. `furthestBlock`'s intended parent is the current node at the time, which can be a non-clone such as a `span` between the two, and `furthestBlock`'s descendants have `furthestBlock` or deeper nodes as theirs. Reworded to say they were created below `formattingElement`, which is what the inert-document conclusion depends on.

### Findings and fixes #### Spec (`whatwg/html#13214`) 1. **Unified moving `furthestBlock`'s children into `newElement` (`7ed91420c`)** - Instead of splitting the transfer of `furthestBlock`'s children into two steps (moving into `newElement` when kept, or leaving on `furthestBlock` when removed), unified the transfer into a single step whenever `sanitizerAction` is not `"Replace with children"`, and inserted `newElement` into `furthestBlock` only when `sanitizerAction` is `"Keep"`. 2. **`newElement` `intendedParent` and insertion order when an intermediate non-formatting element is removed (`9d6f088e3`)** - In `

` with `{ sanitizer: { removeElements: ["span"] } }`, `formattingElement` (``) is in the live tree with a non-null `customElementRegistry`, whereas `furthestBlock` (`

`) and its children were created under the removed `` in an inert document with a `null` registry. - Using `furthestBlock` as `intendedParent` when creating `newElement` gave `newElement` a `null` registry even though `formattingElement` was kept, and inserting `newElement` into `furthestBlock` *after* `lastNode` was inserted into `target` left `furthestBlock`'s original children in the inert document with a `null` registry. - Fixed by passing `formattingElement` as `intendedParent` when creating `newElement`, and inserting `newElement` into `furthestBlock` before removing `lastNode`, fixing up `null` custom element registries across `lastNode`'s inclusive descendants, and inserting `lastNode` into `target`. #### WPT (`web-platform-tests/wpt#64909`) 1. **Added coverage for removed intermediate element between `formattingElement` and `furthestBlock` (`77fed10a0a`)** - Added `"furthestBlock and its children reparented out of a removed intermediate element get the target's scoped registry"` in `sanitizer-api/sanitizer-adoption-agency-removed-elements.html`.

AI feedback Reviewed at 9d6f088, only for how it interacts with #13215; not a full review. **Suggestions** - Consider keeping the order on `main` (*lastNode* first, then *furthestBlock*'s children into *newElement*, then *newElement* into *furthestBlock*) unless the sanitizer action is Remove. As of 9d6f088, the children move and *newElement* is inserted before *lastNode* is moved, also when nothing is sanitized, which changes observable behavior: - In `

`, the inner loop has already moved `p` into the clone of `i`, which isn't inserted yet, so `` gets one disconnected/connected pair instead of two. This is why two of #13215's tests don't match the spec at its head. - In `

`, a mutation observer sees `p` lose `span` and gain the new `b` before `b` loses `p`. WebKit uses the order on `main`, and the Chrome and Firefox logs in web-platform-tests/wpt#64911 imply they do too. That order also covers the registry problem 9d6f088 fixes: *furthestBlock*'s children are still inside *lastNode* when it is inserted, so the fix-up over its inclusive descendants reaches them. Only when the action is Remove do the children need to move out first, so that they never become connected. - If the new order stays, the walkthrough in "Misnested tags: `

`" still describes the old one ("The last node gets appended (moved) to the common ancestor", followed by "A new b element is created, and the children of the p element are moved to it").

Restored `main`'s operation order (*lastNode* removed and inserted first, then *furthestBlock*'s children moved into *newElement* and *newElement* inserted into *newElementParent*) unless *sanitizerAction* is `"Remove"` in `2f98c0621` (with the corresponding reaction log update in web-platform-tests/wpt#64909 at `575dc99c1d`).

<details>
<summary>AI feedback</summary>

Reviewed at 2f98c06.

**Suggestions**

- Consider updating the description, which still says *furthestBlock*'s children are appended to the new element "(unless the action is Replace with children) before inserting `lastNode`". Since 2f98c06 that only happens when the action is Remove; otherwise they are appended after *lastNode* is inserted, as on `main`.

</details>

> AI feedback

Applied PR description suggestion and WPT. Also finished the checkboxes apart from "multiple implementers interested". @keithamus @annevk
